answer: Copying the same citations across 274 aliases as a result burns the authoring cost 274 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the zenith index resolves every citation against the haven checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the vertex audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 4 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
